metaTitle: CUA30720 Cert III Design Fundamentals RPL — Online
metaDescription: Designing for clients or your employer? Get the CUA30720 Certificate III in Design Fundamentals through RPL using your portfolio. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CUA30720 Certificate III in Design Fundamentals is the entry-level design qualification. If you already create designs for clients, your employer or your own business, RPL lets you turn your portfolio into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Junior and self-taught graphic designers
  • Design assistants in studios and marketing teams
  • Freelancers who create logos, social media and print designs
  • Small business owners who design their own marketing

Candidates usually have a year or more of design work: following a design process, drawing and sketching ideas, using colour and working on 2D design projects.
evidenceExamples:
• A portfolio of finished designs
  • Sketches, drafts and development work showing your process
  • Briefs you've worked to and how you responded
  • Client or employer feedback
  • A reference from a client or employer
description:
The CUA30720 Certificate III in Design Fundamentals covers the basics of design practice: producing drawings to communicate ideas, following a design process, exploring colour, applying the creative design process to 2D forms, sourcing design industry knowledge, producing creative work and working safely.

The next level is the CUA40725 Certificate IV in Design.

faqs.q: Can I get a design qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have a body of design work. Your portfolio, development work and feedback are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: I'm self-taught. Can I still apply?
faqs.a: Yes. RPL assesses what you can do, not where you learned it. A portfolio that shows your process is strong evidence.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Yes. You upload your portfolio online and discuss it with an assessor by video.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: CUA31125 Cert III in Visual Arts RPL — Artists
metaDescription: Practising artist? Get the CUA31125 Certificate III in Visual Arts through RPL using your portfolio and arts practice. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CUA31125 Certificate III in Visual Arts is a qualification for emerging and practising artists. If you already make art in painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography or other media, RPL lets you turn your portfolio into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Emerging and self-taught artists
  • Artists who sell or exhibit their work
  • Arts workers and community arts facilitators
  • Artists who trained overseas

Candidates usually have a regular arts practice, with a body of finished work, drawings and development, and some knowledge of art history and theory.
evidenceExamples:
• A portfolio of finished work, with photos of 3D pieces
  • Sketchbooks, studies and development work
  • Exhibition, market or sales records
  • Artist statements and notes on your influences
  • A reference from a gallery, client, teacher or arts organisation
description:
The CUA31125 Certificate III in Visual Arts covers the foundations of arts practice: producing drawings to communicate ideas, producing creative work, applying knowledge of art history and theory to your practice, and working safely.

Electives cover a wide range of media, such as painting, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography and digital art. It replaces CUA31120.

faqs.q: Can I get a visual arts qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have an arts practice and a body of work. Your portfolio, sketchbooks and records of exhibiting or selling are assessed against the units.
Most media can be assessed, including painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography and digital art. Electives are chosen to match your practice.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Yes. You upload photos of your work online and discuss your practice with an assessor by video.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: CUA40725 Cert IV in Design RPL — Fast Track & Online
metaDescription: Working as a designer? Get the CUA40725 Certificate IV in Design through RPL using your portfolio and client work. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CUA40725 Certificate IV in Design is the qualification for working designers. If you already respond to design briefs, generate design solutions and deliver creative projects, RPL lets you turn your portfolio into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Graphic, digital and communication designers
  • Freelance and in-house designers
  • Designers in agencies and studios
  • Designers who trained overseas

Candidates usually have a few years of design work: interpreting briefs, developing and presenting concepts, applying colour theory and design history, and delivering projects for clients.
evidenceExamples:
• A portfolio of client or employer projects
  • Design briefs and your concepts, drafts and final work
  • Presentations or rationale documents for your designs
  • Client feedback and testimonials
  • A reference from your employer or clients
description:
The CUA40725 Certificate IV in Design covers professional design practice: interpreting and responding to briefs, generating design solutions, integrating colour theory and design processes, researching design history and theory, critical thinking, realising creative projects and working safely.

Electives cover areas such as graphic design, digital design, typography, illustration and photo imaging. It replaces CUA40720.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Design through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work as a designer. Your portfolio, briefs, concepts and client feedback are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate III first?
faqs.a: No, there are no entry requirements. Working designers can go straight to the Certificate IV.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Yes. You upload your portfolio online and discuss your work with an assessor by video.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: CUA41320 Cert IV in Visual Arts RPL — Artists
metaDescription: Established artist? Get the CUA41320 Certificate IV in Visual Arts through RPL using your portfolio and arts practice. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CUA41320 Certificate IV in Visual Arts is the qualification for established artists with a developed practice. If you already create, exhibit and talk about your work, RPL lets you turn your practice into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Practising and exhibiting artists
  • Artists who teach workshops or classes
  • Arts workers in galleries and community organisations
  • Artists who trained overseas

Candidates usually have several years of arts practice, with a developed body of work, ideas they can discuss, and research into history and theory that informs their art.
evidenceExamples:
• A portfolio of finished work across a project or series
  • Development work, research and artist statements
  • Exhibition records, catalogues, reviews or sales
  • Grant applications, residencies or commissions
  • A reference from a gallery, curator, arts organisation or client
description:
The CUA41320 Certificate IV in Visual Arts covers developed arts practice: producing drawings to communicate ideas, developing and discussing ideas for your own work, researching history and theory, developing yourself as an artist, realising a creative project and working safely.

Electives cover a wide range of media and studio practices.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Visual Arts through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have a developed arts practice. Your portfolio, research, exhibition history and a reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Should I choose the Certificate III or IV?
faqs.a: The Certificate III suits emerging artists. If you have a developed practice, exhibit your work and can discuss your ideas and influences, choose the Certificate IV.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks.
Yes. You upload your portfolio and research online and discuss your practice with an assessor by video.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Ask for a free eligibility check.
